transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-11-18
Time: 15:00 UTC
Scheduled duration: 52 minutes (recorded)
Attendees: Evan Chen (Redwood AE), Priya Singh (SE), Avery Reed (CS), Lena Park (Legal Ops) — Redwood; Maria Lopez (Procurement), Daniel Kim (Legal), Olivia Zhang (Cloud), Samir Rao (Finance), Jaya Patel (Security) — PivotalEdge

Auto-summary (auto):
Short: Procurement + legal intake to align contracting path for MSA/DPA, confirm SLA floor and pricing gating, evaluate private deployment options and next steps for procurement committee.
Topics: MSA exception paths, DPA redlines (data residency & subprocessors), SLA uptime tiers and credits, pricing approval process, on-prem/VPC options, benchmarking needs.

--- Transcript ---
[00:00] Evan Chen: Hey everyone — thanks for joining. we'll do a quick intro, then run through the MSA/DPA items and where you need approvals for pricing. I think we have about 50 minutes, so try to keep q's tight.
[00:12] Maria Lopez: Hi all, Maria from procurement. we are the primary gate for vendor onboarding, want to make sure we cover the approval path.
[00:18] Daniel Kim: Daniel, legal. I skimmed the MSA, have a few exceptions that may be non-standard for us.
[00:22] Priya Singh: hey, Priya — SE at Redwood. I'll cover technical constraints, private deployment feasibility and SLA implications on architecture.
[00:29] Olivia Zhang: Olivia — clouds. we'll want to see network diagrams and egress cost estimates.
[00:33] Evan Chen: Great. quick agenda — 1) contracting flow and redlines, 2) SLA targets and service credits, 3) pricing gating and procurement timelines, 4) private/VPC options and tech checklist, 5) next steps.

[02:05] Daniel Kim: On the MSA: section 6.2 around subcontractors — we need a clear list of subprocessors or a clause to require notice. also limitation of liability cap — our risk team usually wants it to be 3x fees and carve outs for gross negligence.
[02:22] Lena Park: Evan, is the current MSA copy the standard Redwood template or the enterprise one? I saw two.
[02:28] Evan Chen: This was the standard enterprise template — but we can route the enterprise version with options. We also have a DPA separate doc. I'll send the redline we usually use for healthcare customers.
[02:40] Maria Lopez: For procurement, we need to know which clauses are negotiable and which are showstoppers. timeline wise, the pricing committee meets on 2025-11-26. ideally we have a final commercial sheet before then.

[03:10] Priya Singh: on SLA: from a runtime perspective, we offer tiers. we can do 99.9% or 99.99% depending on Dedicated vs Hosted and regional redundancy. latency SLOs are a separate bucket — are you expecting 100ms p95 for inference?
[03:28] Olivia Zhang: 100ms p95 is our target for user-facing features, but we could accept higher for batch workflows. need to understand cost delta.
[03:36] Samir Rao: cost is a big gating item for finance. any SLA uplift should have an explicit cost per QPS or committed spend delta.

[04:15] Priya Singh: absolutely. quick callout: Dedicated capacity with pinned GPUs and cross-region replication is typically what buys 99.99% and lower tail latency. Hosted can reach 99.9% with warm pools and burst. We can quantify costs — I'll take an action.

[05:02] Daniel Kim: About data residency — we need logs and any customer data to remain in EU/US-only regions. DPA needs to specify no cross-border transfer unless with SCCs or contractual mechanism. Does Redwood support per-customer region pinning for hosted?
[05:21] Evan Chen: yes, we offer region pinning for hosted for some models/regions. For Private/VPC deployments obviously you control the region. We'll mark that in the DPA redline.

[06:00] Jaya Patel: Security — we need KMS/HSM integration, separation of access for logs, audit logging retention of 7 years, and a SOC2 report. We also want to see encryption at rest keys per-customer.
[06:15] Priya Singh: KMS integration is supported for Private and Dedicated; hosted supports customer-managed keys in certain plans. We can share SOC2 cert and pen test summary.

[07:00] Maria Lopez: procurement process question: do we need an executed MSA before the pricing committee can approve? Or can procurement provisionally approve pending DPA finalization?
[07:12] Evan Chen: procurement can provisionally approve commercial terms, but legal generally wants DPA + MSA alignment before final signature. we've done conditional approvals before — we can provide commercial sheet now and redlines shortly.

[08:10] Olivia Zhang: on VPC peering: for private deployments, what's the networking footprint? Do you require a dedicated subnet and peering? what's the egress pattern?
[08:20] Priya Singh: we support three patterns: 1) dedicated VPC + peering (recommended for lowest blast radius), 2) private endpoint (managed NAT), 3) on-prem appliance for air-gapped. Egress depends on model serving (if telemetry is sent to control plane) — we'll put a topology doc.

[09:00] Evan Chen: I'll add a link to the network topology in the notes — small diagram and typical ports.

[10:05] Samir Rao: can you provide a pricing delta between hosted standard and dedicated reserved capacity? need ballpark per GPU per month or per-token estimates.
[10:18] Priya Singh: yes — short version: Hosted is pay-as-you-go with per-token; Dedicated is committed GPU pool — lower per-token at scale but requires monthly/annual commit. If you give me expected QPS and concurrency, I can model it.

[11:30] Maria Lopez: timeline recap — procurement wants the commercial sheet by 11/21 to prep for pricing committee on 11/26. legal wants DPA redline before 11/21 ideally. Is that feasible?
[11:42] Evan Chen: we can do that — Priya and I will push redlines and a commercial summary.

[12:10] Daniel Kim: a couple specific redline asks: 1) data deletion windows after contract termination (we prefer 30 days with certification), 2) breach notification SLA of 72 hours, 3) limitation of liability exceptions for IP claims.
[12:30] Lena Park: Redwood's standard is 90 days for deletion but we can do 30 for healthcare customers — depends on the deployment mode. I'll note that as negotiable.

[13:00] Jaya Patel: do you allow on-prem deployments with HSM integration? we have stricter requirements and prefer customer-managed keys.
[13:08] Priya Singh: yes — on-prem package supports HSM/KMS and fully air-gapped installs. there are additional support and licensing terms for that option.

[14:00] Evan Chen: ok team, let's talk SLA credits — typical structure is a percentage rebate or service credits tied to monthly uptime. We can map three tiers.
[14:18] Priya Singh: Tier A (Hosted standard): 99.9% uptime — 10% credit for monthly below; Tier B (Dedicated): 99.95% — 20% credit; Tier C (Dedicated + cross-region): 99.99% — 30% credit. This is illustrative — legal/finance will want fixed numbers.

[15:02] Samir Rao: that's helpful. finance also wants to model worst-case credits annually to see exposure. Evan, can we get numbers in cash terms?
[15:10] Evan Chen: yes — Priya will produce a notional example of monthly charges vs credits.

[16:00] Olivia Zhang: for the pricing committee, we need to show comparative TCO: Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private for 12/24 month horizons. can Redwood provide a spreadsheet?
[16:12] Priya Singh: I'll prepare a three-scenario sheet and include assumptions for token counts, QPS, and latency targets.

[17:05] Daniel Kim: on indemnity — we typically require indemnification for third-party IP claims. does Redwood have a standard IP indemnity clause?
[17:18] Evan Chen: yes. we have a standard IP indemnity; we can share it. we'll mark any carve-outs.

[18:00] Maria Lopez: procurement notes — approval path: 1) commercial sheet to pricing committee, 2) procurement gating for insurance and org-vet, 3) final legal signoff. Is vendor due diligence needed? we do security questionnaire and SIG.
[18:15] Jaya Patel: yes, we'll need an updated SIG and our vendor risk team will run rapid assessment. we may request SOC2 and pen test evidence.

[19:05] Evan Chen: we'll attach SOC2 cert and latest pen test summary to the folder.

[20:00] Olivia Zhang: a nit — does Redwood support private endpoints that avoid internet egress for inference requests? That would materially lower our compliance concerns and egress costs.
[20:12] Priya Singh: yes, private endpoints and VPC peering are supported for Dedicated/Private. hosted private endpoints are in limited regions — I'll call that out.

[21:45] Daniel Kim: about DPA subprocessors — can you provide a list and commit to notice 30 days before adding new subprocessors?
[21:55] Lena Park: we can commit to notice for major subprocessors; for smaller infra additions we have operational constraints. We'll propose a 30-day notice plus option to escalate to legal if customer objects.

[23:00] Maria Lopez: procurement question on billing: will Redwood invoice monthly, and is net-30 typical? Also any early-termination fees?
[23:12] Evan Chen: monthly invoicing with net-30 is standard. Dedicated reserved capacity has minimum commitment and early termination fees for annual contracts — can be structured. We'll include sample terms.

[25:00] Samir Rao: can we get a sample invoice layout and tax treatment? we need that for our AP team.
[25:08] Evan Chen: yes — I'll include a sample.

[27:00] Priya Singh: quick technical note — if you require 100ms p95 and 1k concurrent requests, we recommend a Dedicated pod with n GPUs; I'll approximate in the sheet. also prefix caching helps, but for user-facing interactive calls caching is less effective.

[28:22] Olivia Zhang: does Redwood support model pinning and versioning so we can freeze model for compliance tests?
[28:30] Priya Singh: yes — model pinning is supported and we can create a freeze snapshot for a release. we also have eval tooling to detect regressions.

[30:00] Evan Chen: quick recap before we move to next steps — action items: we'll circulate DPA redline, commercial sheet, network topology, SIG and SOC2 artifacts. Customer to provide must-have legal items and list of required SLAs.

[31:15] Daniel Kim: one more: encryption key handling — we will need contract language that ensures keys are customer-managed for private deployment.
[31:28] Lena Park: agreed, we'll add options for CMK (customer-managed keys) in the DPA/appendix for Private.

[33:00] Maria Lopez: timeline check again — if we get the docs by 11/21 we can aim for pricing committee on 11/26 and then procurement will do final review week of 11/27.
[33:12] Evan Chen: sounds good. We'll push to that schedule.

[35:00] Olivia Zhang: can you include an example of how service credits are calculated? need a formula, not just percentages.
[35:10] Priya Singh: yes — example formula will be in the SLA matrix — monthly uptime calculation and credit formula (credit = % of monthly fee times X). I'll include examples.

[36:20] Samir Rao: do you have any reference customers in healthcare? a reference would help the procurement steering committee.
[36:28] Avery Reed: yes, we have a couple — I can coordinate a short reference call or written reference.

[38:00] Daniel Kim: outstanding legal ask: audit rights — we usually require the ability to audit subprocessors or get independent report. Is that acceptable?
[38:12] Lena Park: we can provide third-party audit reports and limited audit rights — scope to be discussed. we'll draft language.

[40:00] Maria Lopez: any non-negotiable procurement requirements? For example, minimum insurance?
[40:10] Evan Chen: Redwood carries CGL and cyber coverage; we'll share the certificates. If you require higher limits, we can discuss commercial adjustments.

[41:30] Priya Singh: technical follow-up — if you'd like, we can run a short PoC on Hosted with a traffic replay to produce latency numbers; that helps quantify credits exposure.

[42:00] Olivia Zhang: that could work. what's the time to run a traffic replay?
[42:08] Priya Singh: we can spin a replay in a week if you provide logs and payloads; otherwise we can run a synthetic bench.

[44:00] Evan Chen: ok, final recap and next steps: 1) Evan to send annotated MSA + DPA redline + commercial sheet by 11/21 (Evan). 2) Priya to deliver SLA matrix + pricing scenarios + perf notes by 11/25 (Priya). 3) Customer to provide legal must-haves and network topology by 11/24 (Customer). 4) Schedule follow-up engineering deep-dive if PoC is required week of 11/24 (Evan/Priya).

[45:30] Maria Lopez: thanks, that works. please mark doc links in calendar invite.
[45:40] Evan Chen: will do. I'll also attach SIG and SOC2.

[46:00] Daniel Kim: one small clarification: are we allowed to redline the MSA before the committee or do you prefer to receive comments consolidated?
[46:10] Lena Park: consolidated comments are easier; but Daniel, feel free to redline and send — we'll respond.

[47:40] Jaya Patel: security will run the SIG and likely come back with questions. we may request an architecture workshop.

[49:00] Olivia Zhang: ok that's all from my side.
[49:05] Evan Chen: great. thanks everyone — we'll follow up with the deliverables.
[50:00] Meeting end.

- Evan Chen: send annotated MSA + redline DPA + commercial sheet, SOC2 cert, sample invoice — due 2025-11-21
- Priya Singh: deliver SLA options matrix, pricing scenarios, benchmark notes — due 2025-11-25
- Customer (Maria/Olivia/Daniel): provide legal must-haves, network topology, list of non-negotiables — due 2025-11-24

End of transcript.
